summary: BYD's third-generation Tang launches with a drive-by-wire digital chassis, while the Galaxy M8, Jetour Huanyouzhe EV, Aeolus L8+ and other new models arrive in quick succession, making smart-driving compute power and safety accessibility the year-end battleground for the auto market.

articles.title: BYD Launches Third-Generation Tang: Wire-Controlled Digital Chassis Debuts, Starting at 187,900 Yuan
articles.summary: BYD's flagship SUV, the third-generation Tang, has officially launched at a starting price of 187,900 yuan, debuting wire-controlled digital chassis technology.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, BYD's third-generation Tang has recently gone on sale, starting at 187,900 yuan. The model's biggest technical highlight is its wire-controlled digital chassis — a technology previously seen mainly in high-end vehicles and concept stages, which BYD has now brought down to mainstream price-point products. The wire-controlled chassis replaces mechanical linkages with electrical signals, enabling faster and more precise steering and braking control, while providing the execution-layer foundation for advanced intelligent driving. As the third-generation model in BYD's Tang family, the new car continues the series' SUV positioning while attempting to use chassis intelligence as a differentiating selling point. With competition in the mid-to-large SUV market turning increasingly white-hot, BYD's decision to compete on underlying execution technology signals a roadmap of extending from its three-electric advantage toward full-vehicle intelligence. The 187,900-yuan starting price also brings wire-controlled chassis technology into the consumer sightline of the 200,000-yuan segment for the first time.
articles.impact: The migration of wire-controlled chassis technology from the high end down to the 200,000-yuan market could trigger a new round of arms race among domestic brands in chassis intelligence, accelerating the widespread adoption of intelligent-driving execution-layer technology.

articles.title: Galaxy M8 Opens Pre-Sales: 53kWh Battery as Standard, From CNY199,800
articles.summary: Geely Galaxy M8 pre-sales start at CNY199,800, featuring a standard 53kWh battery and a large five-seat layout, targeting long-range family users.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Geely has officially opened pre-sales for the Galaxy M8, with prices starting at CNY199,800. All variants come standard with a 53kWh traction battery and a large five-seat layout, clearly targeting the long-distance travel needs of larger families. As plug-in hybrid and range-extended SUVs typically use entry-level trims to lower prices and reserve larger batteries for higher trims, the Galaxy M8's decision to make a big battery standard is a differentiated product strategy. The five-seat layout offers advantages in rear-seat space and trunk volume over seven-seat configurations, and combined with the long electric range from the 53kWh battery, covers both daily electric commuting and hybrid long-distance travel. The pre-sale price drops directly below CNY200,000, putting it in head-to-head competition with rivals in the segment.
articles.impact: The standard big-battery approach disrupts the industry norm of small batteries in base trims, potentially raising the configuration benchmark for new-energy SUVs around the CNY200,000 level and improving perceived value for consumers.

articles.title: Jetour Roamer EV Launched: Urban Light-Off-Roader Box-Shape EV From CNY89,900
articles.summary: The Jetour Roamer EV has officially launched at CNY89,900, featuring an urban light-off-road boxy EV design.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the Jetour Roamer EV has recently launched, priced from CNY89,900. The vehicle adopts the trendy "boxy" design, positioned as a pure-electric model with an urban light-off-road style. Boxy designs have continued to gain momentum in the domestic market in recent years, trickling down from hardcore off-roaders to urban commuter cars and becoming an exterior style symbol for younger consumers to express individuality. The Jetour Roamer EV enters this niche with a starting price of CNY89,900, notably lower than competing fuel and new-energy products in the same style. Its light-off-road positioning means it is not designed for serious off-road scenarios, but rather for urban commuting and weekend suburban trips on light unpaved roads. The launch further enriches Chery Jetour's new-energy product lineup.
articles.impact: A boxy EV under CNY90,000 entering the market squeezes the small SUV segment and could accelerate the spread of the light-off-road style in the entry-level market.

articles.title: Dongfeng Aeolus L8+ Launched: From CNY129,900 With 700 TOPS ADAS Compute
articles.summary: The Aeolus L8+ launches at CNY129,900 with 700 TOPS smart-driving hardware, bringing advanced driver assistance down to the CNY130,000 level.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Dongfeng Aeolus has officially launched the L8+, priced from CNY129,900, with smart-driving hardware delivering 700 TOPS of compute. Computing power of this class had previously appeared mostly in mid-to-high-end new-energy vehicles priced above CNY200,000; its appearance at the CNY129,900 price point means advanced ADAS hardware is accelerating its move downmarket into the entry-level segment. Compute power is one of the key metrics supporting complex smart-driving functions such as urban navigation assistance and automated parking, and high on-board computing headroom leaves room for future software iterations and OTA updates. Through the L8+'s class-above smart-driving configuration, Dongfeng Aeolus is attempting to create a memorable selling point based on intelligence in the fiercely competitive compact segment.
articles.impact: The arrival of a 700 TOPS vehicle at the CNY130,000 level will pressure rivals at the same price to close their ADAS gaps, significantly speeding up the democratization of advanced smart-driving hardware.

articles.title: Mercedes-Benz Recalls Again in China: Nearly 180,000 Vehicles Affected
articles.summary: Mercedes-Benz has launched a new recall in China involving nearly 180,000 vehicles, a relatively large-scale action.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Mercedes-Benz has recently launched another recall in the Chinese market, this time involving nearly 180,000 vehicles. As the luxury brand with leading sales in China, Mercedes-Benz has conducted multiple recalls in recent years due to various issues. This recall of nearly 180,000 units will require corresponding dealer service resource allocation and owner notifications. Under domestic regulations, the cost of remedying defects for recalled vehicles is borne by the manufacturer, and consumers can check whether their vehicles are affected through official channels. Large-scale recalls by luxury brands once again underscore the ongoing pressure on product quality management as production and sales volumes expand, and test the responsiveness of automakers' after-sales systems.
articles.impact: The large-scale recall may affect Mercedes-Benz's brand image and after-sales resources in the short term, but standardized recalls also help improve industry quality transparency and consumer protection.

articles.title: AUDI Marks Two Years: Next Chapter of New Energy Unfolds
articles.summary: The AUDI brand marks its second anniversary, with officials saying a new phase for its new energy products has begun.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the AUDI brand has reached the important milestone of its second year since launch, with stakeholders saying the next chapter of its new energy journey has already begun. Serving as a key vehicle for Audi's electrification push in China, the AUDI brand has been tasked with exploring China-specific new energy products and user engagement models since its establishment. Statements made at the two-year mark signal that the brand has moved from its start-up phase into a stage of product and market expansion. Amid unprecedentedly fierce competition in China's new energy vehicle market, traditional premium brands broadly face multiple challenges, including reshaping brand perception, localizing product definitions, and innovating channel models. The AUDI brand's path over the past two years and its plans for the next stage are seen as a case study for tracking the direction of international automakers' electrification strategies in China.
articles.impact: AUDI entering a new phase reflects a shift from testing the waters to doubling down on electrification in China, as competition in the premium new energy segment intensifies.

articles.title: XPeng Robot Demonstrates Untethered Real-Time Interaction: Embodied AI Leaves the Lab
articles.summary: XPeng's robot achieved real-time interaction without remote control on site, showcasing the responsiveness of embodied intelligence technology.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, XPeng's robot performed real-time interaction without remote control at an event, drawing widespread attention. Unlike typical pre-programmed demos or teleoperated systems, untethered real-time interaction requires the robot to rely on its own perception and decision-making systems to instantly interpret the environment and human instructions and respond accordingly — placing higher demands on the combined capabilities of algorithm latency, environmental perception, and motion control. In recent years, XPeng has steadily advanced the joint development of robotics and intelligent driving technologies, with the visual perception and decision-making capabilities accumulated through autonomous driving regarded as a key asset for transfer to embodied intelligence. The live demonstration was a public technical showcase of XPeng's robotics business.
articles.impact: The spillover of automakers' technical capabilities into embodied intelligence is emerging as a new trend, with robotics potentially becoming a second growth curve for smart car companies.

articles.title: US Tech Stocks Extend Pullback: Nvidia's 7%+ Drop Ripples Across the Smart Driving Supply Chain
articles.summary: US tech stocks continued their pullback, with Nvidia falling more than 7% in a single session, pressuring valuations of AI computing-related assets.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, US tech stocks have continued to pull back recently, with Nvidia's single-day decline exceeding 7%. As the world's leading supplier of AI computing chips, Nvidia's stock swings not only affect capital markets' valuation of the AI industry but also indirectly influence sentiment across the smart driving supply chain. Many automakers currently position advanced intelligent driving as a core selling point, while high-computing chips and cloud-based training capacity are critical inputs for smart driving R&D. Against the backdrop of the tech stock pullback, capital markets may become more cautious about the 'burning cash for smart driving' business model, and automakers' cost control and monetization pace in intelligent driving investment will face greater scrutiny. However, short-term stock volatility does not change the long-term technological direction of automotive intelligence.
articles.impact: Volatility in AI computing asset valuations could affect the financing and investment pace of the smart driving supply chain, pushing automakers to focus more on the commercialization efficiency of smart driving technology.

articles.title: Road Test: Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine Delivers Just 3.6L/100km Fuel Consumption
articles.summary: The Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine recorded a real-world fuel consumption of just 3.6L/100km, taking the hybrid efficiency race to a new level.
articles.detail: NetEase Auto road test data shows that the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine variant achieved a real-world fuel consumption of only 3.6L/100km. The figure is highly competitive among same-segment gasoline and hybrid SUVs, reflecting the technical strength of the Blue Whale powertrain in thermal efficiency and energy management. For family buyers, fuel economy is one of the most sensitive long-term cost factors in the purchasing decision, making real-world data more meaningful than rated figures. As new-energy vehicle penetration continues to rise, efficient hybrids and ultra-low-consumption gasoline technology remain the practical choice for the large number of users without home charging access. Changan is reinforcing its efficiency brand through powertrain labels such as the Blue Whale Super Engine to counter the squeeze from plug-in hybrids and range-extended models on the traditional gasoline SUV market.
articles.impact: Real-world fuel consumption at the 3.6L level strengthens the Blue Whale powertrain's reputation, providing data support for Changan's dual-track strategy in hybrid and high-efficiency gasoline technology, and directly affecting the pricing strategies of rival models in the same segment.

articles.title: CCTV Interviews AIVA's Li Bo: Deconstructing the Product Logic of AI-Native Vehicles
articles.summary: In a CCTV interview, AIVA's Li Bo breaks down how AI-native vehicles rebuild product definition and user experience from the ground up.
articles.detail: NetEase Auto reports that CCTV recently interviewed AIVA's Li Bo for an in-depth discussion on the product logic of AI-native vehicles. An AI-native vehicle refers to one whose architecture is designed around AI capabilities from the very start of product definition, rather than layering smart features onto a conventional vehicle. Such products differ from traditional models in interaction modes, the pace of feature iteration, and data closed-loop systems. At a time when multiple automakers are competing to market intelligent driving and smart cabins as key selling points, the AI-native approach implies a more fundamental product restructuring, involving wholesale changes to the electrical and electronic architecture, software platform, and user operations system. CCTV's attention to the topic also reflects how the convergence of AI and the auto industry has become an industry-wide issue.
articles.impact: The spread of the AI-native concept will push automakers from "feature stacking" toward "architecture restructuring," with software and data capabilities becoming the dividing line for core competitiveness among automakers in the next phase.

articles.title: Safety and Smart Driving Rapidly Going Mainstream: From Changan's 'Safety for All' to 700TOPS at Budget Prices
articles.summary: Safety features and advanced autonomous driving hardware are accelerating their move into mainstream price segments, set to become the main battleground in the next phase of auto market competition.
articles.detail: Taken together with today's multiple reports, the 'democratization' trend in automotive technology is becoming increasingly clear. In a NetEase Auto interview, Changan's Jiang Ping explicitly stated that 'safety should not be tiered by trim level,' advocating universal access to safety technology by opening previously premium-exclusive safety features to buyers across the entire model lineup. Meanwhile, Dongfeng Fengshen L8+ brings 700TOPS of intelligent driving computing power to the 129,900-yuan price point, and BYD introduces a drive-by-wire digital chassis on the third-generation Tang starting at 187,900 yuan. As core capabilities such as safety, chassis intelligence, and high-compute intelligent driving shift from premium exclusives to mainstream standards, consumers' criteria will move from 'is it there' to 'does it work well,' and competition among brands will return to a contest of technology integration and cost control.
articles.impact: Technology democratization will reshape consumer purchase decision criteria, and second- and third-tier brands lacking core technology integration capabilities will face greater pressure for market elimination.

articles.title: The Auto Industry in the AI Wave: From Smart Cockpits to Embodied AI and Capital Rationality
articles.summary: Xpeng's robot demos and discussions on AI-native vehicles run in parallel, while a tech stock pullback pushes the industry into a phase of technology delivery and valuation reshuffling.
articles.detail: From Baidu's trending search featuring Xpeng's robot performing real-time interaction without remote control, to a CCTV interview with AIVA's Li Bo discussing the product logic of AI-native vehicles, to the pullback in U.S. tech stocks with Nvidia down over 7% causing volatility in computing asset valuations, today's information sketches the dual face of the auto industry's deep entanglement with AI: on one hand, technology capabilities continue to spill over and product forms keep evolving, with new species such as robots and AI-native models emerging at an accelerating pace; on the other, capital markets are beginning to demand much stricter timelines for returns on AI investment. For automakers, the key going forward lies not in how many AI stories they can tell, but in whether they can convert perception, decision-making, and interaction capabilities into product value that users can feel and sustainable business models.
articles.impact: The auto industry's AI narrative will shift from concepts to delivery, and automakers with both technology deployment capability and cost efficiency will more easily earn recognition from both capital and the market.
